Born in New York on 19 November 1818, son of Dana Hutchins and Olive Smith and grandson of Cyrel.
He married Maryette Briggs on 12 December 1844; she died on 26 May 1861, and on 12 February 1862 he married Amy Avery,
born in 1826 (Hutchins family books) . He was a trustee of the Methodist church at Westville,
by the family book. The censuses from 1850 to 1880 find him farming at Fort Covington,
his land worth $200 in 1850, $1,500 in 1860 and $3,000 in 1870.
In 1860 his household held Maryette, six children from Juliette, 15, and DeWitt,
12, down to Frederick, 4, and his parents Dana and Olive; in 1870 his widowed mother,
72, was still with him. He registered for the Civil War draft at Fort Covington in 1863,
and died there on 13 August 1904. Father of the first DeWitt and of Frederick, who ran the lumber business with him
at Fort Covington. His wife Maryette Briggs was the granddaughter of Lieutenant Henry Briggs,
who enlisted in May 1775, days after Lexington and Concord, and served through the siege of Boston;
Christopher Briggs, her uncle, helped compile the first history of Franklin County.
Born at Trout River, Franklin County, New York, about 1825, daughter of Winchester Briggs,
who owned a saw-mill there, and Nancy Cowan; her grandfather was Lieutenant Henry Briggs of the Revolution.
She married Allen Dana Hutchins on 12 December 1844, and they made their home at Fort Covington.
Their children included Juliette, Almeda, Edwin, George, Frederick and the first DeWitt,
born in 1847. She died at Fort Covington on 26 May 1861, in her mid-thirties, and is buried at Bangor.
